claim: CRISPR is a family of DNA sequences found in prokaryotic organisms like bacteria and archaea.
quote: CRISPR ( / ˈ k r ɪ s p ər / ; acronym for clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats ) is a family of DNA sequences found in the genomes of prokaryotic organisms such as bacteria and archaea.

claim: CRISPR sequences are used to detect and destroy DNA from similar bacteriophages during subsequent infections.
quote: These sequences are used to detect and destroy DNA from similar bacteriophages during subsequent infections.

claim: Cas9 is an enzyme that uses CRISPR sequences to recognize and open specific strands of DNA.
quote: Cas9 (or "CRISPR-associated protein 9") is an enzyme that uses CRISPR sequences as a guide to recognize and open up specific strands of DNA that are complementary to the CRISPR sequence.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 technology can be used to edit genes within living organisms.
quote: Cas9 enzymes together with CRISPR sequences form the basis of a technology known as CRISPR-Cas9 that can be used to edit genes within living organisms.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 has applications in biological research, biotechnology, and disease treatment.
quote: This editing process has a wide variety of applications including basic biological research, development of biotechnological products, and treatment of diseases.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing was recognized by the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020.
quote: The development of the CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing technique was recognized by the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020 awarded to Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna.

claim: CRISPR/Cas system evolved as a bacterial defense mechanism against viruses and bacteriophages.
quote: The CRISPR/Cas system evolved in nature as a means for bacteria to protect themselves from invading viruses and bacteriophages by inserting pieces of their DNA into the host genome.

claim: CRISPR sequences were first described by Ishino et al. in 1987.
quote: The first description of what would later be called CRISPR is Ishino , et al. in 1987.

claim: CRISPR spacers are fragments of DNA from viruses that previously attacked the cell.
quote: In effect, the spacers are fragments of DNA gathered from viruses that previously attacked the cell.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 can introduce site-specific double-stranded breaks in DNA.
quote: The Cas9 endonuclease introduces site-specific double-stranded breaks in DNA, enabling gene inactivation, removal, or insertion through cellular repair mechanisms.

claim: CRISPR and TALENs are core techniques in genome editing.
quote: Transcription activator-like effector nucleases (TALENs) and the Cas9-guideRNA system (adapted from CRISPR) are the two most common.

claim: Genome editing techniques can insert, delete, and modify DNA at multiple levels.
quote: Techniques have been devised to insert, delete, and modify DNA at multiple levels.

claim: Early genome editing techniques used meganucleases and zinc finger nucleases.
quote: Early techniques relied on meganucleases and zinc finger nucleases.

claim: CRISPR-Display is a modification of the CRISPR/Cas9 system using a nuclease deficient Cas9 and engineered sgRNA with aptameric accessory RNA domains.
quote: CRISPR-Display, in contrast, uses a nuclease deficient Cas9 (dCas9) and an engineered sgRNA with aptameric accessory RNA domains.

claim: CRISPR-Display allows investigation of the functionality of long non-coding RNAs and targeting of ribonucleoprotein complexes to genomic loci.
quote: This allows for investigation of the functionality of certain lncRNAs, and targeting of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes to genomic loci.

claim: CRISPR-Display incorporates RNA polymerase II to permit expression of longer transcripts, overcoming RNA polymerase III limitations.
quote: CRISPR-Display incorporates RNA polymerase II to permit expression of longer transcripts (~80–250 nucleotides) to overcome this limitation.

claim: CRISPR-Display can deploy large RNA domains to genomic loci, enabling control of gene expression.
quote: CRISP-Disp allows deployment of large RNA domains to genomic loci.

claim: CRISPR-Display was developed by David M. Shechner, Ezgi Hacisuleyman, Scott T. Younger, and John Rinn at Harvard University and MIT.
quote: CRISPR-Display was first published in Nature Methods in July 2015, and developed by David M. Shechner, Ezgi Hacisuleyman, Scott T. Younger and John Rinn at Harvard University and MIT.

claim: CRISPR gene editing is a genetic engineering technique that modifies the genomes of living organisms.
quote: CRISPR gene editing...is a genetic engineering technique in molecular biology by which the genomes of living organisms may be modified.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 enables in vivo genome editing and is precise, cost-effective, and efficient.
quote: The technique is considered highly significant...as it enables in vivo genome editing and is considered exceptionally precise, cost-effective, and efficient.

claim: CRISPR can be used to create new medicines, agricultural products, and genetically modified organisms.
quote: It can be used in the creation of new medicines, agricultural products, and genetically modified organisms.

claim: CRISPR offers potential in treating inherited genetic diseases and diseases from somatic mutations like cancer.
quote: It also offers potential in the treatment of inherited genetic diseases as well as diseases arising from somatic mutations, such as cancer.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 can introduce knock-in mutations via homology-directed repair (HDR).
quote: Knock-in mutations, facilitated via homology-directed repair (HDR), are the traditional pathway of targeted genomic editing approaches.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 can cause knock-out mutations through non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or TMEJ.
quote: Knock-out mutations caused by CRISPR-Cas9 result from the repair of the double-stranded break by means of non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or POLQ/polymerase theta-mediated end-joining (TMEJ).

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 has been experimentally used on non-viable human embryos since 2015.
quote: Since 2015, CRISPR has been experimentally investigated on non-viable human embryos.

claim: The first drug using CRISPR gene editing, Casgevy, was approved in 2023 for sickle-cell disease and beta thalassemia.
quote: In 2023, the first drug making use of CRISPR gene editing, Exagamglogene autotemcel, sold under the brand name "Casgevy", was officially approved...to cure sickle-cell disease and beta thalassemia.

claim: Genome editing involves inserting, deleting, modifying, or replacing DNA in an organism's genome.
quote: Genome editing , or genome engineering , or gene editing , is a type of genetic engineering in which DNA is inserted, deleted, modified or replaced in the genome of a living organism.

claim: CRISPR gene editing improved the efficiency and specificity of genome editing.
quote: The development of CRISPR gene editing in 2015 improved the efficiency, specificity, and practicality of large-scale genome editing.

claim: Genome editing has been experimentally investigated on non-viable human embryos since 2015.
quote: Since 2015, genome editing has been experimentally investigated on non-viable human embryos.

claim: The CRISPR-Cas system was selected as the 2015 Breakthrough of the Year by Science.
quote: The CRISPR-Cas system was selected by Science as 2015 Breakthrough of the Year.

claim: Genome editing can be used to create pigs resistant to porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome.
quote: The University of Edinburgh Roslin Institute engineered pigs resistant to a virus that causes porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome.

claim: CRISPR gene editing was safely tested on cancer patients in a US trial in 2020.
quote: In February 2020, a US trial safely showed CRISPR gene editing on 3 cancer patients.

claim: Genome editing can be used to create plants with enhanced nutritional properties, like the Sicilian Rouge High GABA tomato.
quote: In 2020 Sicilian Rouge High GABA, a tomato that makes more of an amino acid said to promote relaxation, was approved for sale in Japan.

claim: Genome editing can be used for gene therapy by replacing defective genes with functional ones.
quote: By inserting a functional gene into an organism, and targeting it to replace the defective one, it could be possible to cure certain genetic diseases.

claim: Site-specific recombinases like Cre-LoxP and Flp-FRT are used to study gene functions by knocking out genes.
quote: In order to study the function of these genes, site specific recombinases (SSR) were used. The two most common types are the Cre-LoxP and Flp-FRT systems.

claim: Genome editing relies on DNA double-stranded break repair mechanisms like NHEJ and HDR.
quote: A common form of genome editing relies on the concept of DNA double stranded break (DSB) repair mechanics.

claim: Prime editing is a genome editing technology that modifies the genome by directly writing new genetic information into a targeted DNA site.
quote: Prime editing is a 'search-and-replace' genome editing technology in molecular biology by which the genome of living organisms may be modified.

claim: Prime editing does not require double strand breaks or donor DNA templates for genome modification.
quote: It mediates targeted insertions , deletions , and base-to-base conversions without the need for double strand breaks (DSBs) or donor DNA templates.

claim: Prime editing has potential applications in medical genetics and has been used in animal models, plants, and bacteria.
quote: The technology has received mainstream press attention due to its potential uses in medical genetics. It utilizes methodologies similar to precursor genome editing technologies.

claim: Prime editing involves a fusion protein consisting of a catalytically-impaired programmable endonuclease linked to an engineered reverse transcriptase.
quote: The most basic prime editor uses a fusion protein , consisting of a catalytically-impaired programmable endonuclease linked to an engineered reverse transcriptase.

claim: Prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA) identifies the target nucleotide sequence and encodes new genetic information to replace the targeted sequence.
quote: Prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA) : capable of (i) identifying the target nucleotide sequence to be edited, and (ii) encoding new genetic information that replaces the targeted sequence.

claim: Prime editing can result in a heteroduplex DNA composed of one edited strand and one unedited strand, with nucleotide mismatches at the editing site.
quote: This process allows 3' flap ligation, and creates a heteroduplex DNA composed of one edited strand and one unedited strand.

claim: Prime Editor 3 strategy uses a standard Cas9 nickase to improve editing success by targeting the opposite non-edited strand.
quote: To counter this, the Prime Editor 3 strategy comes with an extra component borrowed from base editing. In addition to the editor itself, PE3 uses a standard Cas9 nickase to exploit DNA repair systems by targeting the opposite non-edited strand.

claim: Prime editor 4 includes a plasmid encoding for dominant negative MMR protein MLH1 to reduce cellular MMR response and increase editing efficiency.
quote: Prime editor 4 utilizes the same machinery as PE2, but also includes a plasmid that encodes for dominant negative MMR protein MLH1.

claim: Twin prime editing (twinPE) allows editing of large DNA sequences, addressing a key drawback of prime editing.
quote: The "twin prime editing" (twinPE) mechanism reported in 2021 allows editing large sequences of DNA – sequences as large as genes – which addresses the method's key drawback.

claim: Engineered pegRNAs (epegRNAs) can increase prime editing efficiency by preventing degradation of the 3' end by exonucleases.
quote: Prime editing efficiency can be increased with the use of engineered pegRNAs (epegRNAs).

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 is a technology for modifying DNA.
quote: use of CRISPR gene editing (CRISPR/Cas9), a technology for modifying DNA.

claim: The He Jiankui affair involved the first use of genome editing on humans.
quote: The He Jiankui affair is a scientific and bioethical controversy concerning the use of genome editing following its first use on humans.

claim: The World Health Organization has issued guidelines on human genome editing since 2019.
quote: The World Health Organization has issued three reports on the guidelines of human genome editing since 2019.

claim: The Chinese government has regulations prohibiting human gene editing and cloning.
quote: the National People's Congress of China passed Civil Code and an amendment to Criminal Law that prohibit human gene editing and cloning with no exceptions.

claim: Human germline engineering involves modifying the genome of germ cells to create heritable changes.
quote: Human germline engineering ( HGE ) is the process by which the genome of an individual is modified in such a way that the change is heritable.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 is a genome editing technique that uses an enzyme and guide RNA to cut DNA at specific locations.
quote: The CRISPR-Cas9 system consists of an enzyme called Cas9 and a special piece of guide RNA (gRNA).

claim: Human germline engineering is prohibited by law in over 70 countries and by an international treaty of the Council of Europe.
quote: HGE is prohibited by law in more than 70 countries and by a binding international treaty of the Council of Europe.

claim: Genetic engineering is widely used in agriculture, distinct from human germline engineering.
quote: Genetic engineering is in widespread use, particularly in agriculture.

claim: Human germline engineering can potentially prevent genetic disorders or modify non-disease traits like height.
quote: Human germline engineering has two potential applications: prevent genetic disorders...and to modify traits such as height.

claim: The CCR5 Δ32 allele can be introduced to human embryos to confer resistance to HIV.
quote: Modifying human embryos to give the CCR5 Δ32 allele protects them from the disease.

claim: Eugenic modifications through HGE can lead to 'designer babies' with selected traits.
quote: Eugenic modifications to humans yield 'designer babies', with deliberately-selected traits.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 is more commonly used in non-human species or cell culture systems than in humans.
quote: Although CRISPR/Cas9 can be used in humans, it is more commonly used in other species or cell culture systems.

claim: The lack of international regulation on HGE has led to calls for an international ethical framework.
quote: The lack of international regulation led researchers to attempt to create an international framework of ethical guidelines.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 is also known as CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing.
quote: Also CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing .

claim: Genetic modification is also referred to as genetic manipulation.
quote: Also genetic modification or genetic manipulation .
